children: Investors flocked to Thursday’s $22B auction of 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds
, drawn by multi-year high yields and mounting expectations of imminent Federal Reserve rate hikes.

The auction generated historically robust demand, with the new securities awarded at 5.308%—nearly three basis points below pre-auction trading levels. Because the bonds were priced lower than anticipated, aggressive bidders shut out investors holding out for higher yields.
Underscoring this fervent appetite, Wall Street primary dealers were left with a record-low 2.2% of the total sale, a key indicator that direct end-investors eagerly absorbed the supply.
This blockbuster auction unfolded against a broader surge in government debt yields, heavily influenced by
prices that threaten to stall disinflation. Following the sale, the 30-year benchmark
touched levels unseen since 2007 around 5.36%, while the two-year note
breached 4.5% for the first time since 2024. The 10-year tenor
also made a new multi-year high at 4.95%.
Consequently, traders are hastily recalibrating their monetary policy outlook. Markets

a roughly 70% probability of a Fed rate hike next week, fully anticipating a move by October. However, for long-term investors, the opportunity to lock in a risk-free 5.3% return for three decades clearly proved too attractive to pass up.

title: 30-year Treasury auction draws strong demand as yields keep climbing
